facts.statement: The holotype fossil is an incomplete anterior upper jaw with teeth discovered in a chalkstone quarry near Langton Matravers.
facts.quote: Plataleorhynchus is based on holotype NHMUK PV R 11957 (earlier BMNH R.11957), an incomplete anterior upper jaw with teeth found in a chalkstone quarry near Langton Matravers.

facts.statement: The genus was named in 1995 by Stafford Howse and Andrew Milner.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 1995 by Stafford Howse and Andrew Milner.

facts.statement: The specimen was held by the Corfe Castle Museum and the Dorset County Museum in the 1950s before being purchased by the Natural History Museum in 1958.
facts.quote: It was previously part of the Corfe Castle Museum and then the Dorset County Museum during the 1950s before the Natural History Museum purchased the specimen in 1958.

facts.statement: The front of the skull expands into a circular, spatula-like shape holding 22 narrow teeth that point sideways.
facts.quote: It is notable because it expands to form a circular, spatula-like shape at the front, holding 22 narrow teeth that point sideways.

facts.statement: The preserved snout contained forty additional tooth sockets, leading to an estimated total of 76 teeth in the upper jaws.
facts.quote: Forty other teeth (sockets) were present in the preserved remainder of the snout; the total for the upper jaws was estimated at 76.

facts.statement: Its skull length was estimated to be at least 40 centimeters, despite being similar in overall size to large gnathosaurines like Gnathosaurus.
facts.quote: Although Plataleorhychus would have been similar in size to large gnathosaurines like Gnathosaurus, its skull length was estimated at a minimum of 40 centimeters (15.75 in),

facts.statement: David Unwin placed it in the subgroup Gnathosaurinae in 2005.
facts.quote: David Unwin in 2005 placed it in the subgroup of the Gnathosaurinae.

facts.statement: A 2025 phylogenetic analysis suggests Plataleorhynchus falls outside the grouping of all other gnathosaurines.

facts.statement: It lived from the Late Jurassic to Early Cretaceous periods (Tithonian to Berriasian stages) in what is now the Purbeck Group of Dorset, England.
facts.quote: Plataleorhynchus is a genus of ctenochasmatid pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Late Jurassic to Early Cretaceous periods (Tithonian to Berriasian stages) of what is now the Purbeck Group of Dorset, England.

facts.statement: Its time range is estimated from 143.1 to 137.05 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Berriasian (143.1 to 137.05 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Researchers suggest it may have stirred up water-dwelling animals from muddy or weedy environments due to its spoonbill shape, a horn-covered palate pad, and small teeth.
rejected.quote: the different shape of its spoonbill, presence of an apparently horn-covered pad on the palate, and smaller teeth suggest it did not feed in the same way, perhaps stirring up water-dwelling animals from muddy or weedy environments.

rejected.statement: It is classified as a member of the Ctenochasmatidae, a group containing many filter feeders.
